1.1.title: Create your free Zapier account

steps.say: Hello, I'm Emeka. In this short clip, you'll create your free Zapier account. It takes about two minutes.
show: Use a fresh browser profile with your business Google account

steps.say: First, open the pricing page. Plans change often, so check the current free plan here. Don't trust a number from a video, not even this one.
show: Check the current free plan on the pricing page

steps.say: Click Sign up, then Continue with Google. Use your business Google account from lesson 0.6, not your personal one.

ui.label: See your name and email address

steps.say: This is the permission screen. Read it before you click Allow. You should know what you are giving.

ui.label: Apps you use: Gmail, Google Sheets

steps.say: Zapier asks a few questions about your work. They only shape the suggestions you see. If you don't know an answer, skip it.
show: Trial offered? Note the day it ends

steps.say: This is your home. You create a Zap here. Your Zaps live under Zaps. Zap history is your debugger. And Apps shows every app you connect.

1.1.end: That's all. Your account is ready. Back in the lesson, you'll build your first Zap, and Tolu's supplier invoices will start filing themselves.

1.1.title: Connect Google Sheets in Zapier

steps.say: Hello, I'm Miracle. In this clip, you'll connect Google Sheets to Zapier for the first time. You do this once, and every Zap can use it.
show: Trigger already tested: New Form Response

steps.say: Add the action. App: Google Sheets. Event: Create Spreadsheet Row.
Under Account, click Sign in, and choose your business Google account.

ui.label: See, edit, create and delete your spreadsheets

steps.say: Now read this list slowly. Zapier is asking to see and edit your spreadsheets. That's what this Zap needs. If you're happy, click Allow.
Pick the spreadsheet and the sheet. Zapier reads row 1, so your columns appear. Map each answer to its column. No columns? Your headers aren't in row 1. Fix the sheet, then Refresh fields.
Test the step, then check the sheet. One new row, every value in its column. And the phone number kept its zero.
show: Phone column formatted as plain text

steps.say: You can see all your connections here. Give this one a clear name, so you never connect the wrong account by mistake.

1.1.end: Connected once, named clearly, and tested. Every Zap can use it now.

1.1.title: Use a Zapier template link

steps.say: Hello, I'm Emeka. Zapier templates come as a link. One click copies the whole Zap into your account. Let's try it with this lesson's invoice Zap.
You can see the steps before you take it: Gmail New Attachment, then Google Drive Upload File. Click Try it.
Now it's a draft in your own account. The steps and mapping came across. The accounts did not. That's good. Nobody's login travels in a link.
show: Steps and mapping copy; logins never do

steps.say: Connect your business Gmail and read the permissions. Then check the trigger: label Invoices, and minus in colon sent, so your own quotes are never filed.
Connect Google Drive. Pick your own Supplier invoices folder. And check the File field uses the file itself, not its name.
show: File = the file, not its name

steps.say: Test the trigger, test the step, then look in Drive. There's the invoice, with a proper name.
Check the name, HL Invoices to Drive, and publish.

1.1.end: Remember: nothing runs until you publish.

2.1.title: Create your free Make account

steps.say: Hello, I'm Miracle. Welcome to the Weave Workshop. In this clip, you'll open your free Make account.
Start with the pricing page. Make counts credits, and plans change. Check the current free plan before you build, and before you advise a client.
show: Check the current plan on the pricing page

steps.say: Sign up with your business Google account, the same one from lesson 0.6. Read the permission screen before you allow anything.
Give your organisation a clear name. If Make asks where to keep your data, choose a region and write it down. A client may care later.
Here are your scenarios, and this button creates a new one. Connections, your saved logins, live here. And this shows your credits. Remember Glitch: every polling check costs a credit.
show: Every polling check costs a credit

2.1.end: Your workshop is open. Next, you'll build your first scenario and watch the bundles move.

2.1.title: Connect Google Sheets in Make

steps.say: Hello, I'm Emeka. Let's connect Google Sheets to Make. You do it once, and every scenario can use it.
Click the big plus. Search Google Sheets. Choose Watch New Rows.
No connection yet, so click Create a connection. Give it a name you'll recognise. Sign in with your business account, read what Make asks for, then Allow.

ui.label: Choose where to start: From now on

steps.say: Choose the spreadsheet and sheet. Yes, the table has headers. Limit, ten rows a run. Then choose From now on. If you choose all, the first run treats every old order as new.
Your connections live here. If Google ever stops working, come here first and verify or reauthorise it.
Save the scenario. Leave scheduling off for now.

2.1.end: In the lesson, you'll add the email module and run it once.

2.1.title: Import a Make blueprint

steps.say: Hello, I'm Miracle. Our Make builds come as blueprints: one file that rebuilds the whole scenario. Let's import one.
Create a new scenario. In the editor's menu, choose Import Blueprint. Pick the file you downloaded, and save.
The modules appear, already joined. A blueprint brings the steps and mapping. It never brings logins. So these modules need you.
Open each module and pick your connection. Where you see YOUR_SHEET_ID, choose your own spreadsheet. A webhook or data store? Click Add and create your own.
Same for the email module: your connection, your address.

ui.label: Mrs Adebayo Test · Mr Okafor Test · Iya Basira Test

steps.say: Add three test rows, then Run once. Three bundles, three emails. Click the bubbles to see the data. Unknown module? The template panel lists every one, so build it by hand.
show: Unknown module: use the build list

2.1.end: Save it. Switch scheduling on only when you're happy with the test and the credit estimate.

3.1.title: Start n8n in Docker (or a Cloud trial)

steps.say: Hello again, I'm Emeka. Welcome to the Forge. Today you'll start n8n on your own laptop. First, make sure Docker Desktop is open and running.
This command creates a volume. Think of it as n8n's fridge. Your workflows, credentials and encryption key stay here, even when the container is thrown away.

ui.label: Editor is now accessible via http://localhost:5678

steps.say: Now the run command from Card 3. The port is the door to your browser. The timezone is Lagos. And the volume is connected. Press Enter, and wait for this line.
Open localhost 5678. n8n asks you to create the owner account. It's a local login, but use a strong password anyway, and keep it in a password manager.
show: Strong password, saved in a password manager

steps.say: Skip the optional questions. This is your Forge. Create workflows here. Executions shows every run. Credentials is where logins and keys live. Never type a key into a node.
show: Keys live in Credentials, never in a node

steps.say: Now the test that matters. Stop n8n. Start it again. Refresh the browser.
n8n asks you to sign in, not to set up again. Your data survived. The volume is working.

3.1.end: No Docker? Start an n8n Cloud trial instead, and check the current plan on the pricing page. Either way, you're ready for your first workflow.

3.1.title: Create a Google Sheets credential in n8n

steps.say: Hello, I'm Miracle. Our weather workflow needs to write to Google Sheets. In n8n, that login is called a credential. On your own laptop, it takes a few extra steps.
Under Credential, choose Create new. n8n shows an OAuth Redirect URL. Copy it exactly. This one address causes most Google errors.

steps.screen: Google Cloud · Create OAuth client ID
steps.say: In Google Cloud Console, go to Credentials and create an OAuth client ID. Web application. Name it n8n local. Paste the redirect address, character for character. Then Create.
Google gives you a client ID and a client secret. Treat the secret like a password. Copy each into n8n. Don't save them in a note or send them on WhatsApp.
show: The secret is a password: never share it

steps.say: Click Sign in with Google. You'll see a warning that Google hasn't verified this app. That's expected: it's your own app, in testing. Continue, read, then Allow.
show: Expected for your own test app

steps.say: Connection successful. Name it Google Sheets, and save. If you ever see redirect URI mismatch, copy the address again.
Now the node can see your sheets. Pick HL Weather. Map automatically, because your field names match the headers.

3.1.end: On n8n Cloud, you just sign in with Google. Either way, do this once, and every workflow can use it.

3.4.title: Paste an n8n template

steps.say: Hello, I'm Emeka. Every n8n build in this course is a template you can paste. Click Copy. The whole workflow is now on your clipboard.

ui.label: Click the canvas, then Ctrl+V (Cmd+V on a Mac)

steps.say: In n8n, create a new workflow. Click on the empty canvas, then press Control V. On a Mac, Command V.

ui.label: Schedule Trigger → HTTP Request → Split Out → Edit Fields → Supplier prices

steps.say: Here it is. Always read the yellow note first. It tells you which credential to pick and what to replace.
Templates never carry credentials, so select your own. See YOUR_SHEET_ID in capitals? That's a placeholder. Replace it with your sheet's ID, or pick it from the list.
Check every node for words in capitals with underscores. Here, there are none left.

ui.label: Supplier prices sheet · one row per product

steps.say: Save, then Execute workflow. About four pages come in, Split Out makes about two hundred items, and the sheet fills, one row per product.
When your test passes, publish it, and it runs every morning at seven.

3.4.end: That's every template in this course: paste, pick credentials, replace the capitals, test, publish.

B0.title: Boss 0 demo · The Order Flood blueprint

steps.say: Hello, I'm Miracle. This is a finished Boss 0 blueprint. No tool is running yet, so we test it like a consultant: one real-looking case, walked through every page.
show: One test case through every page

ui.label: Tolu / Admin lane: only if it doesn't fit

steps.say: At 8:40 in the evening, the Grand Palm Hotel emails: add two crates of eggs to tomorrow. It lands in the Automation lane, and it's applied before nine. Tolu only sees it if something doesn't fit.
show: “Please add 2 crates of eggs to tomorrow's delivery.”

steps.say: The change lives in Order_Changes: one row, source email, applied yes or no. The order keeps its own unit price, so a price jump can't rewrite old orders.
Here's the hotel's order as JSON, pasted into the lab from lesson 0.3. Valid. Every field has the type we said it would.
Now the AI step, run once with test data. It returns a change, not a new order: eggs, two crates. Then our checks: is it on the list, is the quantity sensible? Anything odd goes to Tolu.
And the inventory says how it connects: Gmail, polling in the evening, read-only on one label. The secret lives in the platform, never in a document.

B0.end: One case, through every page, with no gaps. Now walk your own test case through yours.

B1.title: Boss 1 demo · The Lead Machine

ui.label: Catch Hook → Filter → AI → Code → Sheets

steps.say: Hello, I'm Emeka. This is the finished Lead Machine. Catch the lead, filter tests, AI reads it, rules score it, the sheet records it, and Paths decide what's next.
Here's a test lead: Grand Oak Suites, a hotel in Bodija, three hundred and fifty thousand naira a week, starting in two weeks. Send.
In Zap history, the run is already there. The AI pulled out the budget and start date. The code, not the AI, gave a score of eight. Hot.
The Leads sheet has the row: score eight, hot, status Contacted.
And the lead's email: their first name, a line from their message, no prices or promises. Just a warm reply and a call coming.
Tolu's alert arrived within seconds, because the trigger is instant.
Now Glitch's test entry. Send. The filter stops it at step two. No AI, no email, no row, no wasted tasks.

B1.end: One hot lead handled in under a minute. Record yours the same way.

B2.title: Boss 2 demo · Receipt-to-Books

ui.label: Gmail → Iterator → AI → Parse → Seen before? → Category rules → Checks → Router

steps.say: Hello, I'm Miracle. This is Receipt-to-Books. Receipts come in, the AI reads them, rules check them, and nothing is ever counted twice.
Test one: a Farmgate Supplies invoice, FG-0192, with VAT.
Run once and watch the bubbles. The AI pulled out supplier, number and lines. Subtotal plus VAT equals total. The rules say Cost of goods. So it goes to Expenses.
Here's the row in Expenses, VAT kept separate. And here's its key in the data store.
Now Glitch's favourite: the same invoice, sent again. Same key, so it stops here, and the log says why. Counted once, not twice.

ui.label: Revenue · Cost of goods · Gross profit · Margin
Net profit · VAT separate · vs last month

steps.say: Finally, the monthly report. It normally runs on the first at seven. Today we run it once on our test month.
Always check one month by hand. Same numbers. Now the accountant can trust it.

B2.end: Bookkeeping support, not tax advice: the accountant still reviews it. Record your demo the same way, ending with the P&L email.

B3.title: Boss 3 demo · The Telegram Order Bot

ui.label: Telegram Trigger → Switch → Customer lookup → Classifier → Extract → Code price → IF

steps.say: Hello, I'm Emeka. This is the finished Telegram Order Bot, on our own server. The AI reads the words. The price list sets the price. Nothing is final until the customer taps Confirm.
show: Prices from the sheet, never the AI

ui.label: Message: 2 crates tomato and 1 big tatashe, tmrw, Bodija

steps.say: I'm a customer in Bodija. I type the way I'd text a friend. Send.

ui.label: 2 × crate tomatoes · 1 × big bag tatashe · ₦34,000 · delivery free

steps.say: In seconds: two crates of tomatoes, one big bag of tatashe, thirty-four thousand naira, delivery free. Tap Confirm, and I get my order number and delivery day.
In the sheet, the order is saved, and the stock went down: tomatoes from fourteen to twelve, tatashe from six to five.
In Executions, you can follow each step of that run. Every message is one execution.

ui.label: Orders · revenue · top products · low stock · waiting

steps.say: The evening report runs at eight. For this demo I run it once by hand. Tolu gets orders, revenue, top products, low stock, and anything waiting for her.

B3.end: Message, summary, Confirm, order row, evening report. That's the demo. Record yours the same way.

B4.title: Boss 4 demo · Sage Desk

ui.label: Guardrails → Agent (4 tools) → Output check → Decision log

steps.say: Hello, I'm Miracle. This is Sage Desk. One agent, four tools, five safety layers. Here are the five moments that prove it's ready.

ui.label: Delivery was 3 hours late. Refund for my tomatoes?

steps.say: One: a policy answer. Sage searches the policy, names the section, and quotes the money rule exactly. No guessing.

ui.label: Sage: out for delivery · rider assigned

steps.say: Two: an order lookup. Sage knows who's asking from Telegram itself, not from anything the customer types.
show: Identity from Telegram, not the message

ui.label: Refund HL-0398 · broken eggs · awaiting review

steps.say: Three: a refund. Sage proposes it and tells the customer it's waiting for review. Tolu sees the order, amount and reason, and approves. Only then does money move, in test mode.
Four: an attack. Customer B tries to give orders. Sage stays polite and says no. The log shows no refund tool was even called.

ui.label: Customer B · wants a person · 3rd late delivery

steps.say: Five: a hand-over. Sage tells the customer when to expect a reply, and Tolu gets three lines: who, what they want, what's been tried. Sage stops until Tolu releases it.

ui.label: policy · lookup · refund approved · attack refused · hand-over

steps.say: Every decision, logged.

B4.end: Policy answer, order lookup, approved refund, attack refused, hand-over. That's the demo.

B5.title: Boss 5 demo · Growth Desk

steps.say: Hello, I'm Emeka. This is Growth Desk: six engines, one customer record, one report, and Tolu in control. Six quick moments, all with test accounts.
One: a prospect. The draft uses one verified fact from the restaurant's own website. Tolu approves on her phone, and only then does it send, from the outreach subdomain.

ui.label: Comment: how much for a basket?
Private reply with price list price

steps.say: Two: a comment becomes a lead. Growth Desk replies privately with the price from the price list, and saves the lead with its source.
Three: one customer, two channels. One customer record, one answer, on the latest channel.
Four: the newsletter. Checked against approved offers, approved by Tolu, sent only to people who said yes. Unsubscribe works on every channel.
Five: the CRM fills itself. Company, contact, deal and source. People move the stages. The workflow never does.

ui.label: Leads by source · response times · cost per customer

steps.say: Six: the Monday growth report, run once now. Leads and customers by source, response times, and what each new customer costs.

B5.end: Find, answer, nurture, track, measure. All inside each platform's rules. That's Growth Desk.

6.4.title: Grand Capstone demo · Harvest Lane on Autopilot

steps.say: Hello, I'm Miracle. This is Harvest Lane on autopilot: thirteen workflows on three platforms, one map, one events log. Let's follow one order, in test mode.

ui.label: 2 baskets of tomatoes and 1 crate of eggs to Bodija

steps.say: A customer in Bodija orders on WhatsApp. Within a minute: the price, from the stock table, and a Paystack payment link.
The customer pays. This is Paystack test mode, with Paystack's test card. No real money moves.
Payment verified, so the nearest free rider gets the job on Telegram. The rider taps Accept, then Delivered, and the customer is told at each step.
Now the question an investor will ask: what happened to this order? One order ID, one timeline, across every workflow. And stock went down by itself.

ui.label: Orders · payments · deliveries · needs you · all ran ✓

steps.say: Every morning at half seven, Tolu gets this. Ten seconds to read. Orders, payments, deliveries, what needs her, and whether every workflow ran.

6.4.end: Errors, silences and wrong answers are all watched. And Tolu can run it without us. That's the capstone.
